Gmnotes: Script: Teach only the minimum rules, then move on. Open the GM Rules Drawer for deeper questions, but do not dump the full rulebook before play. Every rules term should link to the GM Rules Drawer in GM view. Do not present non-official or stale mechanics as official Daggerheart rules. Checklist: Duality Dice explained; Hope/Fear explained; Experiences explained; Helping explained; Outcome matrix explained Rules snapshot: Duality Dice; Hope; Fear; Action Rolls; Experiences; Helping; Difficulty Ladder; Combat Spotlight Difficulty: easy 10; standard 15; hard 20
Gmscript: Teach only the minimum rules, then move on. Open the GM Rules Drawer for deeper questions, but do not dump the full rulebook before play.

Gmreadaloud: Here is the minimum Daggerheart loop. Tell me what your character wants to do. If the outcome is risky, uncertain, or dramatic, I will ask for a roll. Most rolls use two d12s: one Hope die and one Fear die. You add the right trait from your sheet and compare the total to a Difficulty. The total tells us whether you succeed. The higher die tells us whether the result comes with Hope or Fear. Doubles are a Critical Success. You do not need to remember all of that right now; I will walk you through it when the first roll happens.
Gmchecklist: Duality Dice explained Hope/Fear explained Experiences explained Helping explained Outcome matrix explained
Playertakeaway: Players know the minimum Daggerheart loop: describe action, roll when risky, read Hope/Fear.
Storytakeaway: The system supports cinematic choices and consequences rather than tactical homework.
Mechanictakeaway: Teaches Duality Dice, Hope/Fear, traits, Experiences, Stress, HP, Armor, and spotlight at a high level.

Takeawayhelp: Players know the Daggerheart loop Players know describe action, roll when risky, read Hope or Fear. Minimum loop: fiction first, dice second, total for success, higher die for Hope/Fear, doubles for Critical Success. "Tell me what you do. If it is risky or uncertain, roll two d12s, add the right trait, and tell me the total and which die is higher." If someone asks what Hope and Fear mean: "Hope means the result tilts toward you and you may gain Hope. Fear means the result gives me a GM resource or complication."
